title: Build the model's parameters from two tables

blocks.text: The feeder team exports its candidate projects as two CSV files, and the selection model needs three of its parameters from them. For each project $`i \in P`$:
and, for each child project $`c \in C`$, its parent $`p(c)`$. A project whose parent cell is blank is not a child.
Write `model_inputs(projects, npv)` in `inputs.py`. It returns three dicts keyed by project id: `capex`, `value`, and `parent` (child id to parent id, children only).

items: `projects` has the columns `project_id`, `cost_profile` (yearly costs joined by `;`, for example `300;200`), `earliest_start` and `parent`.
`npv` is long: the columns `project_id`, `start_year` and `npv`, one row per project and start year.

blocks.text: Both frames come straight from `pd.read_csv` with no `dtype=`, as the team's loader reads them, so every column has the type pandas guessed for that file.

from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd


def model_inputs(projects: pd.DataFrame, npv: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[dict, dict, dict]:
    """Return (capex, value, parent): three dicts keyed by project id."""
    capex = {pid: sum(int(c) for c in str(profile).split(";"))
             for pid, profile in zip(projects["project_id"], projects["cost_profile"])}
    npv_at = npv.set_index(["project_id", "start_year"])["npv"].to_dict()
    value = {pid: npv_at[pid, start] for pid, start in zip(projects["project_id"], projects["earliest_start"])}
    children = projects[projects["parent"].notna()]
    parent = dict(zip(children["project_id"], children["parent"]))
    return capex, value, parent


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import io
    projects = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO("project_id,cost_profile,earliest_start,parent\nA,100;50,2030,\nB,70,2031,A\n"))
    npv = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO("project_id,start_year,npv\nA,2030,210\nB,2031,95\n"))
    print(model_inputs(projects, npv))

cases.says: each project's capex is the sum of its yearly costs
each project's value is its NPV for a start in its earliest start year
a file whose profiles are all one year long, so pandas reads the column as integers, gives the right capex
the NPV table's rows may come in any order
a later start with a higher NPV does not change a project's value
a project with a blank parent cell is not in the parent dict

origin.section: Turn Each Table Into the Sets and Dicts the Model Indexes

concepts: a blank cell reads as NaN, which an if treats as true, so missing values are found with notna
a long table keyed by two columns becomes a dict keyed by pairs, which is how a model indexes a two-index parameter
